title: acceptor-thread-exhaustion-and-rate-thresholding-draft-2026-09-12
content:
SUMMARY:

This is a working draft post-incident note for the outage window on 2026-09-12 that impacted hosted API streaming and some non-streaming endpoints for ~27 minutes. Impact pattern: intermittent client timeouts followed by tenant-scoped 5xx errors for a subset of high-throughput customers.

High level (TL;DR):
- Root cause (preliminary): acceptor thread pool exhaustion on edge streaming frontends combined with aggressive per-tenant rate-thresholding logic that moved failing requests into a fast 503 path.
- Immediate mitigation: rolling restart of affected frontends + temporary relaxation of per-tenant thresholding; removed a buggy guard in the rate limiter that accelerated fail-open behavior.
- Next actions: patch acceptor backpressure handling, add instrumentation and alerting for acceptor-queue-length, revisit threshold heuristic for bursty tenants, update runbook to include steps for graceful drain/restart of streaming frontends.

IMPACT:
- Start: 2026-09-12 01:14 UTC, End: 2026-09-12 01:41 UTC (total ~27m)
- Symptoms: elevated p95/p99 latency on streaming accept endpoints; TCP connections in SYN-RECV / ESTABLISHED but not progressing; clients observed stall then 5xx on subsequent calls.
- Affected: ~12 tenants saw increased 5xx rates, high-volume tenants experienced partial session disconnects. No data loss reported; requests that hit 5xx were not accepted.
- Business: degraded UX for real-time features; SRE pager fired P0.

DETECTION AND ALERTING:
- First signal: internal streaming latency alert (p99 > 900ms) fired at 01:13:58 UTC.
- Secondary: custom connection-accept-latency alert triggered at 01:14:05 UTC (new metric added in July).
- Pager rotation: L1 on-call (Liam) acknowledged at 01:14:12 and began triage.

TIMELINE (detailed notes, messy):
- 01:13:58 - p99 streaming latency alert.
- 01:14:05 - acceptor-accept-latency alert. Observed backlog in acceptor queue via edge/acceptor metric.
- 01:14:20 - L1 collects logs: repeated "acceptor: backlog_size=1024" warnings, threads stuck in epoll_wait.
- 01:15:10 - Confirmed rate-limiter moved calls to fast-fail 503 for tenants exceeding threshold; however backlog existed for tenants well below configured steady-state thresholds.
- 01:16:00 - Heap/profile capture triggered on one affected frontend; pprof shows increased goroutine count and many goroutines blocked on acceptor mutex.
- 01:18:00 - Decision to roll restart a small subset of frontends (canary) to confirm impact; canary recovered immediately and backlog cleared.
- 01:22:00 - Rolling restart across all affected frontends completed, traffic normalized.
- 01:24:00 - Re-enabled normal rate-limiter behavior after temporary relaxation.
- 01:41:00 - Postmortem triage call.

INVESTIGATION DETAILS:
- Logs: edge frontends emitted repeated warnings: "acceptor backlog_size=%d" and occasional "acceptor: stalled-connection-id=%s" lines.
- Metrics: acceptor_queue_length increased linearly starting 01:10 UTC, peaking ~1024 on some frontends. Accept-rate to worker pool remained steady, indicating acceptor problem rather than downstream saturation.
- Tracing: traces for stalled requests show long queuing in acceptor stage, no further RPCs downstream.
- Heap/profiler: goroutine dump shows many goroutines blocked on a shared acceptor mutex while performing TLS session extraction. Root cause points to a regression introduced in PR 2867 that changed a lock granularity around TLS session cache lookup.
- Config/rollouts: PR 2867 (merged 2026-09-08) introduced an opportunistic optimization to deduplicate TLS session lookups but accidentally moved a per-connection operation under a global mutex. This was fine under lower concurrency but with high bursty connection churn caused the acceptor thread pool to block.

WHY DID RATE-THRESHOLDING WORSEN IMPACT?
- Our per-tenant rate-thresholding has a heuristic that, when accept latency exceeds X and a tenant shows repeated errors, it rapidly moves traffic to a fast-fail path to protect downstream.
- Because the acceptor backlog was global but thresholding operates per-tenant, tenants that were not the root cause still tripped the fast-fail path due to delayed retries/fanned retries, amplifying 5xx counts.

CONTRIBUTING FACTORS:
- Recent change (PR 2867) reduced lock granularity incorrectly -> global mutex during TLS session lookup.
- No existing alert for acceptor mutex contention or TLS-session-cache lock hold time.
- Rate-threshold heuristic too aggressive under global queueing scenarios.
- Runbook lacked explicit guidance to check acceptor_queue_length and to prefer canary restarts before global restarts.

SHORT-TERM MITIGATIONS (what we did during incident):
- Canary restart of affected frontends to validate restart fixes acceptor backlog (01:18 UTC).
- Rolling restart of remaining frontends (01:19-01:22 UTC).
- Temporarily relaxed per-tenant rate-thresholding (disabled fast-fail path) to prevent collateral 5xx amplification (01:24 UTC).
- Reverted the lock change in a hotfix branch (PR 2891) to be deployed after post-incident validation; noted we shipped a revert candidate to staging immediately.

LONGER-TERM FIXES (planned):
1) Code: revert global mutex change or re-implement with sharded locks and microbench coverage for connection churn patterns. Owner: Diego. ETA: 2026-09-19.
2) Observability: add acceptor_mutex_lock_time metric, and a percentile alert (p99 lock hold > 50ms). Owner: Maya. ETA: 2026-09-16.
3) Rate limiter: change heuristic to consider global acceptor queue signals before aggressive tenant fast-fail; add cooldown window. Owner: Aisha. ETA: 2026-09-23.
4) Runbook updates: add step to check acceptor_queue_length, guidance to canary restart streaming frontends, and checklist for rate limiter relaxation. Owner: SRE runbook working group. ETA: 2026-09-18.
5) Release gating: add synthetic churn test to preprod that simulates TLS handshakes at burst rates; run as part of canary gating for frontends. Owner: Serving runtime QA. ETA: 2026-10-01.

ACTION ITEMS (tracked in JIRA):
- SRE-4219: Add acceptor mutex metrics and alerts. (Maya)
- SRE-4220: Patch and revert PR for TLS session lock change, write tests. (Diego)
- SRE-4221: Update rate limiter heuristics and add integration test. (Aisha)
- SRE-4222: Runbook edits + on-call training note. (Liam)

RUNBOOK CHANGES (draft snippets):
- Detection section: check acceptor_queue_length, accept-latency, tls-session-cache-lock-time. If acceptor queue > 512 -> consider canary restart.
- Mitigation section: steps to canary restart: 1) pick two frontends in different AZs, 2) cordon and drain, 3) restart service, 4) validate acceptor_queue drops and p99 latency returns to baseline before moving to next batch.
- Rate-limiter rollback: feature flag path to disable tenant fast-fail policy quickly. Ensure feature flag toggles are audited.

OPEN QUESTIONS / NOTES TO SELF:
- Why did the mutex contended path only surface under today's churn pattern? Was there a change in client behavior or a skewed traffic pattern? Need to correlate with tenant traffic spikes.
- Are there other places in edge code where TLS session cache lookups were moved under new globals? Do a code grep.
- We should evaluate switching to RCU-style caches or lock-free lookups for session extracts.

COMMUNICATIONS:
- Customer comms: CS drafted a message for affected tenants (CS-2405). We suggested retry/backoff client-side while we rolled restarts.
- Internal: Slack incident channel archived SLACK:C04SRE-acceptor-thread-incident; postmortem to be posted to Confluence with link to this draft.

POST-INCIDENT RETROSPECTIVE NOTES (raw):
- Good: Canary restart validated fix quickly and reduced blast radius; hotfix revert path existed and was fast to produce.
- Bad: missing low-level metrics for lock contention; rate-limiter heuristic had unintended coupling to global infrastructure state.
- Process improvement: include acceptor/backpressure checks in the standard streaming incident checklist.

REFERENCES:
- JIRA: SRE-4219 (metrics), SRE-4220 (code revert), SRE-4221 (rate-limiter), SRE-4222 (runbook)
- GitHub PRs: 2867 (introducing change), 2891 (revert candidate)
- Slack: SLACK:C04SRE-acceptor-thread-incident channel logs

NEXT STEPS (this week):
- Owners above to create PRs for code/metrics/runbook.
- Post final postmortem to Confluence once all root cause tests pass and fixes are merged.
- Schedule a 30-minute walk-through with Eng + SRE next Thurs to go over design changes for TLS session handling.

-- end of draft --
